text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 5.5% today, extending a sharp four-day decline from $414.65 to $373.86. The timing tracks with escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East—Iran targeted U.S. military sites in Kuwait on November 18, the same day the stock dropped sharply, while the IEA warned the Strait of Hormuz (a critical oil chokepoint) has lost credibility as a reliable corridor. Paradoxically, U.S. crude remains relatively modest at $89.53 per barrel, suggesting markets may not yet be pricing in sustained supply disruption, but refiners like MPC can face margin pressure if geopolitical risk keeps buyers wary despite adequate current supply.

The backdrop matters: U.S. refineries are running at 95.7% capacity with oil storage normal at 694 million barrels, so the selloff isn't driven by immediate supply crisis or refining stress. Instead, the market appears to be rotating away from energy stocks on broader fear, or pricing in the possibility that escalating Gulf tensions could eventually tighten crude availability and complicate margins in weeks ahead.
